Do you believe that the Croats from Vitez would only shoot at the Croatian part of the village and not at the Muslim part of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: Well, what was their interest in destroying themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me turn to my colleagues to ask whether they have any questions that they want to ask. Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness DM. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: When they came to you to take you to the youth detention centre of Prnjavor, did they choose some people or were they taking everybody, every Croat, to the centre? Was there a choice of certain people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: All Croats who had not left on time, all of them were taken. I mean, all who did not escape from these events on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So all the Croats were taken from the village, from Poculica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: All who had not fled earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Regardless of the age? Did they take people, for instance, who are within a certain age or even old men? You are not an old man, but did they also take older men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: Everybody. The old, the sickly. Everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did they say why? Did they say why you were being taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: Well, they didn't say why. That was a war. That's the way it is in a war. And people then never explain to their victims why they are taking them away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mentioned that -- or at least I take the interpretation, you said there was no love lost between the Croats and the Muslims. And at the same time, you mentioned that Muslim neighbours brought you food when you were in, I suppose, in detention, and that this man, Nasid Bektas, sheltered the women and so on. Does this confirm what you say about -- that there was no love lost between Muslims and Croats, at least from the side of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: I said that relations were normal. We lived together, but we didn't exactly like each other very much. But there was nothing else they could do. I mean, I thanked this Dzidic Muhamed and Nasid and I continue to thank them for their thoughtfulness towards us, their kindness, and Nasid once came to see me and he had something to do in Vitez, and I took him where he was supposed to go because he didn't dare go on his own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I quoted you as saying relations now are not good. That was the translation in English. So do you think you can still live together now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: Life together in the future is difficult. When the dead cannot lie in peace at cemeteries, what will happen to the living? That I do not understand. Because they even disturbed the peace of the dead. They won't let them lie in peace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness DM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Witness DM, I want to talk to you briefly about the man who shot open the door of the building in which you were and who, in doing so, killed some of your companions and wounded others. What happened with that man? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: We don't know who shot and we don't know -- I mean, somebody had to know. And what happened, well, that is only something that the people who were in charge know. We have no way of knowing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, let us talk about Poculica and Ahmici. How far is Ahmici from Poculica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: If you take the road, it's about eight kilometres, but as the crow flies, it is less, up to five kilometres; if you were to take shortcuts too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: If there were explosions at Ahmici, would you hear the sound of the explosions from where you were at Poculica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: Well, you can hear it at a five-kilometre distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: But you said the first sounds which you heard coming from an automatic rifle were heard by you at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: That's what I heard in my own yard, when this guy came to pick me up and then he shot a few bullets so that he would see how everybody would react.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Before that, did you hear any sounds coming from explosions at Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: Well, around that time, I could hear perhaps small arms but, you know, there are several villages out there, so I could not notice exactly where this was happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well then, do I take it that your testimony is that before 9.00, you heard the sounds coming from Ahmici or the surrounding villages and deriving from shells or guns? How would you react to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: I didn't hear shells. Guns, rifles, you could hear them from afar, but I could not tell where from. It was from the yard that I heard this. As they were taking me out, that's when I heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Are there any Muslims now in Poculica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: There are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And no Croats now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DM
utterances.text: No. No Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness DM. Your evidence is over. You have been very courageous. The Tribunal thanks you for having come and wishes you Godspeed back to your village in the hope that everything will become peaceful and, once again, the Trial Chamber thanks you. We are going to escort you out of the courtroom, but I would like everyone to remain for a short Status Conference in closed session. The registrar will ask for closed session and, at the same time, we can take the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 12.44 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 27th day of November, 1998, at 9.45 a.m.
